issues.reason: Complements of nouns and adjectives bars Possession precisely here — "never Possession for an argument", with the genitive reserved for "a true relational noun ... where no underlying verb exists" — and "visit" passes the verb-paraphrase test, while Light verbs over event-nouns makes the event-noun's witness the eventuality itself, so a thematic role on sk_visit_1 is the licensed encoding, not a defect.

gaps_confirmed: a measured distance between two entities ("about 100 miles northeast of Chicago") — Measure is one-place, so the relatum Chicago is severed from the magnitude and MoreBy is comparative, not separational

the possessive SUBJECT of an event nominalization ("Jackson's visit") — the Complements section covers only a nominalization's of-phrase object, and nothing states that an 's possessor may fill a thematic role on the event-noun witness
new_gaps: a temporal-succession verb ("followed") has no route to the canonical Before ordering — it reifies as an ordinary event, so "which happened first?" cannot bind
no rule for whether a period noun used as an event-noun witness ("a night in Benton Harbor") may take the event-side Location oblique rather than entity-attached LocatedIn
notes: The reviewer's own q2 gap 2 concedes the rules are silent on an 's subject of a nominalization, so q1 mistakes gap territory for a defect; the calibration line protects (Agent sk_visit_1 jackson), which is true and well-typed. The severed one-place distance Measure is the parse's weakest atom, but the reviewer correctly filed it as a gap rather than an issue.
